clue.text: Feature of a ruminant found in the field

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for a plant that grows in meadows

indicators.note: 'feature of a ruminant' puts the feature after its owner, so the owner's word comes first in the answer

parts.note: a cow is the classic cud-chewing ruminant; the possessive gives the plural-looking letters
a lip is a feature of the face

explanation.surface: A naturalist notes some part of a grazing animal turning up in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Feature of a ruminant' as a cow's lip: COWS then LIP. The flower name is defined loosely by where it grows.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow wild primula that grows in meadows and pasture.

clue.text: Flighty partner?

parts.note: flighty usually means fickle, but here it means involved in a flight: the second person sharing the controls of an aircraft

explanation.definitionFit: A co-pilot is the colleague who shares the flying of an aircraft with the captain.

clue.text: Dancing girl down under

parts.note: a girl's name with a dance word, set in Australia: the famous Australian bush ballad

explanation.definitionFit: The bush ballad is Australia's unofficial national song; its title pairs a dance with a girl's name.

clue.text: The French have an unfinished article, a strip of wood

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A French publication can't finish its article about a strip of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts the last letter from THE, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A lath is a thin narrow strip of wood, as used under plaster.

clue.text: Deal that needs to be tied up

definitions.meaning: a set of terms agreed together

definitions.text: that needs to be tied up
definitions.meaning: a parcel waiting to be wrapped with string

explanation.definitionFit: A package is both a bundle of agreed terms and a wrapped parcel tied with string.

clue.text: Bird indicating canine happiness

definitions.meaning: what a happy dog does with its tail, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: The wagtail is a small bird; a dog wags its tail when pleased.

clue.text: Satisfactory, and it comes out in the Wash

definitions.text: it comes out in the Wash
definitions.note: a phrase standing for a river that flows into the Wash

parts.note: well can mean in good health or satisfactory, as in 'all is well'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something satisfactory, and it all comes out in the wash, as the proverb says.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a large bay on England's east coast; the River Welland flows into it. The proverb 'it'll all come out in the wash' disguises this.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welland is a river of eastern England whose mouth is in the Wash estuary.

clue.text: The purpose of sport?

parts.note: an aim or target, and also the posts that football players shoot at

explanation.definitionFit: A goal is an aim or objective, and also the target scored into in many sports.

clue.text: Breeder and trainer,'e abused the dog

indicators.note: abused means treated badly, so these words are mangled into a new order

parts.note: the cockney 'e (he with the h dropped) adds a single E

explanation.surface: A dog breeder and trainer are accused of mistreating the animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' rearranges BREEDER, TRAINER and E into the name of a Scottish breed; 'and' joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed, an old name for the Scottish terrier, is a dog.

clue.text: Generosity from a big ship

parts.note: large means big
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Charity coming from a large vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is generous giving, especially of money or gifts.

clue.text: One elected to follow this way of life

definitions.text: One elected to follow this way of life

parts.words: One elected to follow this way of life
parts.note: elected seems to mean chose, but means voted in: an MP's working life

explanation.definitionFit: A working life in government is what someone voted into office takes up.

clue.text: Spend time idly with misplaced zeal

indicators.note: misplaced means put in the wrong position, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lounges around, their enthusiasm gone astray.
explanation.definitionFit: To laze is to idle, doing nothing much.

clue.text: Lacking originality, placing prohibition on a new driver

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
L is the learner plate shown by a new driver in the UK

explanation.surface: Banning a learner from driving is a dull, unimaginative policy.
explanation.walkthrough: UK learner drivers display an L plate, so 'new driver' gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means trite and commonplace, with nothing fresh.

clue.text: Tool which does calculations, it is heard

indicators.note: it is heard signals that the word for doing calculations is spoken, not written

parts.note: adds means does sums

explanation.surface: A gadget that does arithmetic, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it is heard' turns ADDS into the same-sounding tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a cutting tool with an arched blade set at right angles to the handle.

clue.text: Take a partner for better or for worse

definitions.text: Take a partner for better or for worse

parts.words: Take a partner for better or for worse
parts.note: sounds like a dance call, but quotes the wedding vow

explanation.definitionFit: To wed is to take a spouse, with the vow 'for better, for worse'.

clue.text: Musical number?

explanation.definitionFit: A score is the written music of a piece, and also a set of twenty.

clue.text: Carrying capacity of gent on a bender

indicators.note: being on a bender is a drunken spree, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: How much a man can carry when he is out on a drinking binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bender' (a drinking bout) rearranges GENT ON A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage is the cargo a ship can carry, measured in tons.

clue.text: Title of the French musical

parts.note: du is French for of the
Chess is a stage musical by Tim Rice and the ABBA songwriters

explanation.surface: The name of a French stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Duchess is a noble rank, a title held by a woman.

clue.text: Many an Italian region or English county

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100, a large number
Umbria is a region of central Italy

explanation.surface: A list of places that are either Italian regions or English counties.
explanation.walkthrough: C (100) for 'many' is a crossword convention. Cumbria is a county in north-west England, home of the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumbria is a county in north-west England.

clue.text: Not an original way to catch mice?

definitions.text: Not an original way to catch mice?

parts.words: Not an original way to catch mice?
parts.note: an imitator, whimsically seen as a duplicate feline that hunts mice

explanation.definitionFit: A copycat imitates others; the word also suggests a duplicated cat.

clue.text: Examiner who listens?

definitions.meaning: from Latin audire, to hear: a hearer

explanation.definitionFit: An auditor inspects accounts, and literally means a hearer.

clue.text: Woollen yarn was not the best,'e'd concluded

parts.note: worst is the opposite of best
'e'd is he'd with the h dropped, and concluded means it comes at the finish

explanation.surface: A cockney concludes that something was the poorest of the lot.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the h makes he'd into 'e'd, giving ED, which 'concluded' puts at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Worsted is a smooth yarn spun from combed long-staple wool.

clue.text: Know how fewer are out of their mind

parts.note: wit is mental sharpness, the know-how to get things done
less means fewer

explanation.definitionFit: Witless means foolish or crazed, as in 'scared witless'.

clue.text: Prisoners don't enjoy the high life here

definitions.text: Prisoners don't enjoy the high life here

parts.words: Prisoners don't enjoy the high life here
parts.note: the high life means luxury, but here means life up high: a jail cell deep below ground

explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground prison cell beneath a castle.

clue.text: Patrick&Henry's course

parts.note: Pat is short for Patrick
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: The route taken by two men called Patrick and Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a course or route followed.

clue.text: He had shortly arranged to include it for the lady

indicators.note: to include means the shuffled letters wrap round the next word
arranged means put in a new order, so those letters are shuffled

parts.note: he had shortened is he'd

explanation.surface: A man has briefly organised things to make room for it, for her sake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' contracts 'He had' to he'd; 'arranged' reorders those letters to EDH before 'to include' wraps them round IT. 'the lady' is just a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith is a woman's name, so it can stand for a lady.

clue.text: May be about right for some herrings

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: can means may be able to

explanation.surface: A suggestion that something may be correct for a few fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like C for circa, but here it wraps CAN round R. A cran is an old Scottish measure of fresh herrings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cran is a measure of fresh herrings, about 37.5 gallons.

clue.text: Beaten hollow

parts.note: sounds like soundly defeated, but means a hollow made by a blow

explanation.definitionFit: A dent is a depression knocked into a surface.

clue.text: Hit so roughly by child outside

indicators.note: outside means the abbreviation wraps round the jumbled letters
roughly means in a rough way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' gives OS from SO, and 'outside' makes CH (a dictionary abbreviation for child) wrap it. A cosh is a British word for a short heavy club.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosh is to strike with a club or truncheon.

clue.text: Rang for legal aid

parts.note: legal aid sounds like state-funded lawyers, but means help from the law: dialled for officers

explanation.definitionFit: Phoning for officers of the law is summoning help from the force.

clue.text: Disloyal person creates art riot

indicators.note: creates means makes something new from the given letters

explanation.surface: A turncoat stirs up a riot in an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor is someone who betrays their country or friends.

clue.text: Sarah, an eccentric of the desert

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A peculiar woman called Sarah lives in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Saharan means belonging to the Sahara, the great North African desert.
